question.text: If the speed of an airplane is measured in $\textrm{mi/hour},$ what are the units of its acceleration?
question.explanation:
We can find the acceleration of an object by computing the slope of its speed-time graph. So, let's draw an example of a speed-time graph where the speed is measured in $\textrm{mi/hour}$ and the time is measured in $\textrm{hours}.$

In this case, the slope is computed as \[ m = \dfrac{\textrm{change in speed}}{\textrm{change in time}}, \]

and so the units of the slope are as follows: \[ \dfrac{\textrm{units of speed}}{\textrm{units of time}} = \dfrac{\textrm{mi/hour}}{\textrm{hour}} = \dfrac{\textrm{mi}}{\textrm{hour}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\textrm{hour}} = \dfrac{\textrm{mi}}{\textrm{hour}^2} \]

Therefore, the units of acceleration are $\dfrac{\textrm{mi}}{\textrm{hour}^2}.$

question.text: An object accelerates with constant acceleration from $0 \, \textrm{m/s}$ to $20\, \textrm{m/s}$ in $50$ seconds. Find its acceleration.
question.explanation:
We can find the acceleration of an object by computing the slope of its speed-time graph. To plot a speed-time graph, we need two points.

  • The object starts at a speed of $0 \, \textrm{m/s}.$ This corresponds to the point $(0,0).$

  • In $50$ seconds, the car reaches a speed of $20 \, \textrm{m/s}.$ This corresponds to the point $(50,20).$

Since the acceleration is constant, we plot the two points and draw a line through them as follows:

The slope of the object's speed-time graph gives its acceleration. The slope of this line is

\begin{align*} m &= \dfrac{20 \text{ m/s}-0 \text{ m/s} }{50 \text{ s}-0 \text{ s} }\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{20 \text{ m/s} }{50 \text{ s} } \\[5pt] &= 0.4 \, \dfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the acceleration of the object is $0.4 \, \textrm{m/s}^2.$

question.text: The speed-time graph represents the motion of a $250\textrm{cc}$ motorcycle at the start of a race. Calculate the acceleration of the motorcycle.
question.explanation:
In a speed-time graph, the acceleration is given by the slope of the line.

The line passes through the points $(0,0)$ and $(8,28),$ so its slope is: \begin{align*} m & = \dfrac{28 \, \textrm{m/s} - 0 \, \textrm{m/s}}{8 \, \textrm{s} - 0 \, \textrm{s}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{28 \, \textrm{m/s}}{8 \, \textrm{s}} \\[5pt] & = 3.5 \, \dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{s}^2} \end{align*}

Therefore, the acceleration of the $250\textrm{cc}$ motorcycle is $3.5 \, \textrm{m/s}^2.$
